hints: Sort the four names meson, positron, proton and quark by asking which are hadrons, which are quarks, and which belong to the electron family.
Recall that leptons such as the electron, muon and neutrinos are fundamental particles that are not made of quarks and do not feel the strong force.
Recall what a positron is in beta-plus decay - the positively charged antielectron - and decide which family it must share with the electron.
walkthrough: Identify the groups: in 9702 particle physics, matter particles are divided into quarks and leptons, while hadrons such as mesons and baryons are made from quarks.
Recall the lepton members: electron, muon, tau and their neutrinos, plus their antiparticles such as the antielectron.
Check meson: it is a quark-antiquark hadron, so it is not a lepton.
Check proton: it is a baryon hadron made of $uud$ quarks, so it is not a lepton.
Check quark: it is the building block of hadrons and forms its own fundamental group separate from leptons.
Check positron: it is the antiparticle of the electron with the same lepton behaviour but opposite charge, so it is a lepton. This is option B.

options.A: A meson is a hadron made of a quark and an antiquark, not a fundamental lepton.
options.B: A positron is the antiparticle of the electron and belongs to the lepton family.
options.C: A proton is a baryon hadron made of three quarks ($uud$), not a lepton.
options.D: A quark is a separate class of fundamental particle that makes up hadrons, not a lepton.
